Protein Food

Pork Loin

About This Entry

Pork loin is a lean, mild roast from along the spine — tender when not overcooked. Its subtle flavor suits aromatic whites, rosé, and lighter reds with bright acidity rather than heavy tannin.

Beginner Guide

Pork loin is leaner than pork shoulder. Use a thermometer — overcooking dries it quickly. Not the same as tenderloin, which is a smaller, more tender muscle.

FAQ

What is Pork Loin?
Pork loin is leaner than pork shoulder.
How should Pork Loin be cooked?
Lean pork dries quickly — use a thermometer, avoid overcooking, and consider brine or sauce for moisture and wine balance.
